items.headline: Breece Hall (quadriceps) listed as questionable
items.news: Hall (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.analysis: After remaining limited Thursday, Hall stayed capped in Friday's session and will head into the weekend with a chance to make his first appearance since Week 3. If he's cleared to play Sunday, the Jets could have their lead running back available again, though his practice limitations coupled with Braelon Allen's success during Hall's absence keep some uncertainty around the latter's workload.

items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Henderson (illness) did not practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Henderson will try to shed his illness and return to practice Friday. If he's unable to practice without limitations Friday, the 2025 second-round pick would likely take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Henderson has struggled to earn playing time in recent weeks, splitting change-of-pace work behind Rhamondre Stevenson with Corey Kiner.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) listed as questionable
items.news: Barkley (hamstring/back) didn't practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Barkley has yet to practice this week due to dueling hamstring and back issues, the latter of which knocked him out of Monday's loss to the Cowboys. He relayed to Tim McManus of ESPN.com afterward that he isn't concerned about the most recent injury, but he now has just one more chance to get back on the practice field ahead of Sunday's game at Washington. With all of Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) on IR, Jaydon Blue currently is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though the team also used practice squad member Elijah Mitchell in Monday's loss to the Cowboys.

items.headline: Christian Watson (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Watson said he suffered a broken rib in Thursday night's 27-19 win over the Panthers, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Watson took a hard fall in the second quarter after hauling in a 53-yard deep shot from Jordan Love. He landed on the football and was coughing up blood afterward, necessitating a trip to the hospital just before halftime. Scans showed a broken rib, but Watson was deemed fit to return to the game in the third quarter. He'll now have 10 days to rest up before the Packers' next game in Week 9 against the Patriots.

items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.analysis: Going back to last week, Charbonnet now has logged four straight full sessions, indicating that he's drawing closer to his first game action since tearing his left ACL on Jan. 17. Of course, the Seahawks didn't clear him to return this past Sunday against the Chiefs, and rookie first-round RB Jadarian Price (chest) was limited Thursday after the Seahawks designated him for return from IR, throwing another question mark into the potential backfield for Week 8. In any case, Charbonnet will have two more chances to prove his health before Seattle makes a ruling on his status ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

items.headline: Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Jones (hamstring) did not participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Jones exited Sunday night's 20-3 win over Kansas City in the second half with a hamstring injury, and he appears to still be nursing the injury ahead of Week 8. The running back will have two more chances to return to practice before Monday night's contest against the Bears.

items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) listed as questionable
items.news: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Lock remained limited at practice Thursday after logging three straight limited sessions before being ruled out for the team's Week 7 win over the Chiefs. The quarterback has been dealing with an elbow injury, and he will have two more chances to notch a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Bears.

items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.analysis: Shaheed was injured in last Sunday night's win over the Chiefs, but indications are he avoided a serious injury. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Bears, Tory Horton will slot into WR3 duties behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.

items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) listed as questionable
items.news: Burks (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Burks was limited in Wednesday's practice, so it's unclear if his 'DNP' a day later was maintenance-related or the result of a setback. If Burks is available Sunday against the Eagles, he'll have an opportunity to make an impact in a Washington WR corps that has lost receiving yardage leader Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury.

items.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) remains on IR
items.news: Price (chest) was limited in Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.analysis: It was Price's first practice after being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Thursday, which opened the rookie running back's 21-day window for activation. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) potentially set to debut Monday night against the Bears and the presence of both Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, it's difficult to see any of these running backs being reliable fantasy options until/unless the Seahawks pare this backfield down.

items.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Love (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.analysis: Love maintained his activity level from Wednesday, which followed two weeks off due to a lingering ankle injury. Head coach Mike LaFleur hasn't indicated if Love actually has a chance to return to action Sunday at Dallas, but Friday's practice report will reveal his chances to do so.

items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) listed as questionable
items.news: Waddle (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.analysis: Waddle departed in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's win at Arizona due to a chest injury, which limited him in practice last Wednesday and Thursday before he returned to a full session Friday and didn't enter the weekend with a designation. This week has been a different story, though, as he kicked it off with a DNP on Wednesday before Thursday's capped session. Friday's injury report will reveal Waddle's chances to suit up Sunday against the Chiefs.

items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Harvey (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Harvey wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so it's unclear if his limitations a day later stem from Denver's initial practice or were the result of an issue the running back encountered Thursday. In any case, added context with regard to Harvey's status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will arrive no later than Friday. If available this weekend, Harvey will contend with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman for Denver's Week 8 backfield touches.

items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Kelce (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Kelce logged a full practice Wednesday, so the tight end's listed limitations a day later make his status for Sunday's game against the Broncos worth monitoring. He also was limited in practice last week but ended up approaching his team's 20-3 loss to Seattle (in which he caught four of his eight targets for 44 yards) without an injury designation.

items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Rice (hamstring/knee) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Rice has put a pair of limited practices under his belt as he works his way back from a hamstring injury that has sidelined him since Week 4, with a knee injury also in the mix to complicate his recovery. If Rice ultimately gets the green light to face the Broncos, he would likely reclaim his customary role as Kansas City's top wide receiver. He would likely need to log a full practice Friday to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game.

items.headline: Ray Davis (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Davis didn't participate in Thursday's practice due to an illness, Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard reports.
items.analysis: Davis received the day off while he was feeling under the weather, but so long as he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, he should avoid taking a designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens. While handling a backup role behind lead back James Cook this season, Davis has carried just five times for 12 yards to go with three receptions for 40 yards through Buffalo's first six contests.

items.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practice update
items.news: Diggs (hand/hamstring) was a full practice participant Thursday.
items.analysis: Diggs was a non-participant Wednesday due to hand/hamstring/rest, but a return to all activity one day later with 'rest' removed from the injury report indicates the pair of health concerns won't impact his ability to suit up on game days. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season, Diggs will have unfettered access to passes from QB Jayden Daniels moving forward, which so far has ammounted to a 10-99-2 line on 16 targets in their two healthy outings (Weeks 1 and 6) together this season.

items.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Moore (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Moore has been listed as limited both Wednesday and Thursday while practicing in a non-contact jersey. The 29-year-old wide receiver missed Buffalo's last two games prior to a Week 7 bye after having appeared in 92 consecutive regular-season games. Keon Coleman stepped up in Moore's absence and could maintain a larger role Sunday against the Ravens if Moore is ultimately sidelined or limited.

items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) listed as questionable
items.news: Kincaid (chest) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Kincaid has started Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practice sessions coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. The 27-year-old TE has yet to miss a game this season, but Kincaid has cooled down significantly after a scorching start, mustering 90 receiving yards over the past four games after posting 225 yards and a TD through Week 2. Kincaid will look to get back on track Sunday against the Ravens, assuming he plays through the chest injury that's limiting his practice participation.

items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) remains on IR
items.news: Iosivas (thumb) is making good progress in his rehab, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
items.analysis: Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

items.headline: John Bates (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Bates was a non-participant in Thursday's practice due to a shoulder injury.
items.analysis: Bates has been a spectator for the Commanders' first two Week 8 practices and will need to get back on the field in some capacity to put himself in position to play Sunday against the Eagles. The sixth-year tight end has played at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Commanders' first six games, mainly serving as a blocking specialist while recording five receptions for 27 yards on six targets.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Jackson (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Jackson seems on track to return to action for Sunday's game at Buffalo after logging back-to-back uncapped sessions to begin Week 8 prep. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if he's tagged with a designation for that matchup, but the quarterback is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a left high-ankle sprain.

items.headline: Carson Beck (back) injury update
items.news: Beck (back) practiced in full Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.analysis: Beck has been battling a back injury, though it hasn't prevented him from being the team's emergency QB3. While it appears the worst of the injury is behind the rookie signal-caller, that still likely won't improve his chances of getting on the field anytime soon, at least while Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew are healthy.

items.headline: Brenen Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: It was a second consecutive DNP for Thompson, who has been battling multiple injuries for weeks. The 23-year-old was cleared to play in Week 6 versus the Chiefs after missing the three previous games, though he didn't play. It appears Thompson may not be available for the Week 8 meeting with the Rams, especially if he doesn't practice Friday.

items.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Turpin (ribs) was a non-participant in practice Thursday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: Turpin was also a DNP on Wednesday, though that was a walkthrough. The Cowboys held a standard practice Thursday, and Turpin was unable to participate, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday's game against Arizona. Still, Turpin will have a chance to log at least a limited session Friday ahead of the weekend.

items.headline: Jared Wayne (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Wayne (knee) was a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Wayne was also limited Wednesday, so his status for Sunday's clash against New England is hazy. Unless he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, the wideout will likely be tagged with a designation heading into the weekend. In his debut with the Dolphins this past Sunday versus Tennessee, Wayne didn't draw a target on 10 offensive snaps while also playing six snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Ian Thomas (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Thomas (shoulder) was a limited participant at the Raiders' practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Thomas has logged back-to-back limited practices to open the week as a result of a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 7 versus the Rams. The tight end will have one more chance to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

items.headline: Will Kacmarek (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Kacmarek (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Kacmarek has now been limited two straight days to begin Week 8 prep while tending to a hamstring injury. He'll almost certainly enter the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest against the Patriots if he isn't able to practice in full Friday. Kacmarek has worked primarily as a blocker this season, but he does have three catches for 24 yards on six targets through six games.

items.headline: Anthony Gould (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Gould (concussion) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Gould suffered a concussion in the Week 6 loss to the Titans and didn't play versus the Vikings in Week 7. He was estimated as limited in Wednesday's walkthrough, though his full participation in Thursday's practice suggests he will be out there Sunday versus the Jaguars.

items.headline: Drew Ogletree (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Ogletree (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Ogletree hasn't had a productive 2026 campaign, totaling three catches (five targets) for 16 yards. Still, if the knee issue prevents him from suiting up Sunday against Jacksonville, it could at least mean more snaps for Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox behind Tyler Warren (groin).

items.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: Skowronek (calf) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.analysis: Skowronek has missed each of Pittsburgh's past two games due to the calf issue. His ability to begin Week 8 prep with consecutive limited sessions gives the veteran wideout a chance to return Sunday versus Cleveland, though he'll likely carry a designation into the weekend if he's not able to log a full session Friday. When healthy this season, Skowronek has seen limited opportunities on offense, recording just three catches for 32 yards and a touchdown on four targets through five contests.

items.headline: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) practice update
items.news: Chase (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
items.analysis: After sitting out Wednesday's session, Chase assuaged any concerns regarding his availability for Sunday's game against the Titans by practicing without limitations Thursday. The star wide receiver will look to pick up the pace following what has been a slow start by his lofty standards. Chase is averaging a career-low 58.5 receiving yards per game after notching at least 76 yards per game in each of the previous five regular seasons.

items.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Wilson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.analysis: For a second day in a row, Wilson was donning a yellow non-contact jersey on the practice field, and he received the same limited listing as a result. He relayed to Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com on Wednesday that he's tending to sore ribs, but there's been no indication that he's in danger of missing Sunday's game in Dallas. Friday's injury report will reveal if Wilson has a designation ahead of that matchup.

items.headline: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Allen (hamstring) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Allen wasn't listed on the Jaguars' practice report Wednesday, thus he likely picked up the hamstring issue during practice following the team's Week 7 bye. It's unclear how serious the issue is, so the second-year running back's practice participation level Friday should provide clarity about his likelihood of suiting up in Week 8 against Indianapolis. Allen has handled only one carry through six contests, so an absence would primarily affect Jacksonville's special-teams unit.

items.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) listed as questionable
items.news: Allgeier (toe) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.analysis: After Allgeier sat out Wednesday's session due to a toe injury, his ability to mix into drills one day later generally is a good sign as the Cardinals go through Week 8 prep. Friday's practice report will unveil if Allgeier enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, and also whether or not rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has a chance to put an end to a two-game absence. Currently, Bam Knight is the only healthy backfield option on Arizona's active roster.

items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) listed as questionable
items.news: Parkinson (ribs) didn't practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Parkinson has now missed the first two days of Week 8 prep, so his status for Sunday's matchup against the Chargers is looking quite precarious. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to have a chance of suiting up this weekend. Rams QB Matthew Stafford peppered his tight-end corps with 14 targets in Week 7 in the absence of wideout Davante Adams (hamstring), so Parkinson's absence would be felt by the team's offense if he can't play. Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen could be set for a bump in targets if that's the case.

items.headline: Tre' Harris (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Harris (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Harris suffered his hamstring injury in Week 5 against Denver and missed Week 6 ahead of last week's bye. With back-to-back limited practices to open Week 8 prep, Harris has a decent chance of suiting up Sunday against the Rams. In a broken Chargers offense, it's difficult to get excited about anyone on the team for fantasy.

items.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) remains on IR
items.news: Bech (forearm) practiced fully Thursday.
items.analysis: Since being designated for return from injured reserve Monday, Bech has logged consecutive full practices. Should the wideout maintain that level of activity Friday, he'll have a chance to suit up Sunday against the Jets. For that to happen, Bech will need to come of IR by Saturday afternoon. If that transpires, the 2025 second-rounder will have an opportunity to boost a Las Vegas WR corps that has yielded modest production thus far apart from Tre Tucker.

items.headline: Braelon Allen (ankle) practice update
items.news: Allen (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Allen began Week 8 prep as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, but he shed all limitations Thursday, while Breece Hall (quadriceps) remained limited for a second consecutive practice Thursday. Hall got the majority of backfield touches over Allen when both were healthy to begin the season, but the former hasn't seen game action since Week 3. Allen should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Raiders, but uncertainty lingers regarding Hall's status.

items.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Zaccheaus didn't play in the 29-20 win over San Francisco on Sunday. While his limited participation in the Falcons' previous two practices is a positive sign, he still may be heading for an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with Tampa Bay. The 29-year-old hasn't been overly involved this season, catching four passes (11 targets) for 17 yards. However, Zaccheaus plays a role as a return man on special teams, so if he's not cleared to play Sunday, Jahan Dotson and Zachariah Branch may see more action in that capacity, even more so if Brian Robinson (hamstring) is also unavailable.

items.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) listed as questionable
items.news: Ridley (hip) was limited at practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.analysis: The same applies applies to Wednesday's session, giving the wideout one more chance to up his participation level ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals. So far this season, Ridley has recorded just five catches (on 10 targets) for 81 yards in six games, a pace that has kept him off the fantasy radar thus far.

items.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Dulcich (ankle) remained limited at practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Dulcich was also limited at Wednesday's practice, so the tight end likely needs to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Patriots without an injury designation. Dulcich has been targeted five times in each of his last two contests, a span in which he's logged a 9/123/0 receiving line.

items.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: McConkey (concussion) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: McConkey has back-to-back uncapped practices under his belt this week, but it remains unclear if he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires getting the all-clear from an independent neurologist. Friday's injury report will reveal if he still needs to pass such an exam ahead of Sunday's game versus the Rams.

items.headline: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Jones (knee) was limited at Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: In the wake of making an early exit from this past Sunday's win against the Colts after aggravating a knee injury, Jones didn't practice Wednesday, so his return to drills one day later generally is a good sign in the midst of Week 8 prep. Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Detroit.

items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Smith (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Smith so far has sat out Wednesday's walkthrough and Thursday's practice due to a lingering hamstring injury, giving him just one more opportunity to mix into drills this week. The Eagles may make a ruling on Smith's status for Sunday's game in Washington once they post their final Week 8 injury report Friday.

items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) listed as questionable
items.news: Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Monangai hasn't suited up since Week 4, and he continues to be bothered by a pair of injures at the start of Chicago's Week 8 prep. He'll have an extra day to recover with the Bears playing on MNF against Seattle. Roschon Johnson has played in a change-of-pace role behind D'Andre Swift during Monangai's absence.

items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Egbuka (concussion) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Though Egbuka was limited again, he shed the non-contact jersey and worked in a normal practice jersey Thursday. He was still dialed back enough to be listed as limited, but he seems to be making progress as Sunday approaches. Egbuka is working back from a concussion and a foot injury after missing Week 7.

items.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Pickens is dealing with a lingering shoulder issue and a new hamstring injury, which so far has capped his practice reps this week. He'll have one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

items.headline: Brock Bowers (calf) practice update
items.news: Bowers (calf) was a full practice participant Thursday.
items.analysis: Bowers opened Week 8 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a calf injury, but it didn't deter him from returning to all drills one day later. Since making his season debut in Week 3, he's gone for more than 70 receiving yards in all five of his appearances, sitting on a 34-455-3 line on 52 targets on the campaign.

items.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) listed as questionable
items.news: Gainwell (hip) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.analysis: Gainwell returned to practice after sitting out Wednesday's session, but he still faced some limitations Thursday. He'll have one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Friday, and if Gainwell is able to do so, he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Bucky Irving remains atop Tampa Bay's depth chart at running back, followed by Gainwell and Sean Tucker.

items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Brown (ankle/knee) was officially listed as a non-participant at Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Thursday's injury report confirms earlier reporting from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network that Brown isn't practicing Thursday. According to Rapoport, Brown recently had a knee issue flare up, which has the wide receiver's status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins in doubt. Brown has six catches for 75 yards on 16 targets in two games since returning from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.

items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) injury update
items.news: St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: Head coach Dan Campbell told Richard Silva of The Detroit News on Monday that St. Brown tweaked his ankle during this past Sunday's win against the Packers, and while the wide receiver sat out Wednesday's session, he was able to handle a full workload one day later, fulfilling Campbell's prediction. St. Brown thus should be good for the 11.3 targets per game that he's averaged through six appearances this season Sunday versus the Vikings.

items.headline: Malik Washington (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Washington (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: With Washington having now logged limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday, the wideout will look to get back to full participation Friday to clear up any concern about his status heading into Sunday's game against the Patriots. Though he leads the Dolphins in both receptions (26) and receiving yards (289), Washington is coming off a Week 7 outing against the Jets in which he drew a season-low three targets while Miami welcomed back promising rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (2-70-2 receiving line on three targets) from a three-game absence due to an ankle injury.

items.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) listed as questionable
items.news: Warren (groin) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Warren has now logged limited practices on back-to-back days after missing the last two games, a positive sign for his progress ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Despite the two-game absence, Warren still leads the Colts with 30 catches and is second on the team behind Jonathan Taylor with three total touchdowns in five appearances. Warren would likely need to log a full practice Friday to avoid an injury designation.

items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Gibbs (shoulder) practiced fully Thursday.
items.analysis: Gibbs was absent from Wednesday's session due to a shoulder injury, but with his return to all activity one day later, the issue isn't a significant one. He thus should be good to go for his typical 27.7 touches per game that he's averaged through the first six contests of the campaign Sunday against the Vikings.

items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Meyers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Coming out of a bye week, Meyers has had his reps capped in the Jaguars' first two practice sessions of Week 8. The Jaguars haven't indicated that Meyers is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Colts, but if he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, he'll likely head into the weekend without an injury designation.

items.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Robinson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday for the second day in a row, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: Robinson has yet to resume practicing after sitting out Atlanta's Week 7 win over the 49ers due to a hamstring injury. Robinson will likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to avoid being ruled out for a second consecutive game, in which case Khalil Herbert would likely be elevated from the practice squad to work as Bijan Robinson's backup again.

items.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) practice update
items.news: Sampson (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Sampson was limited in the Browns' first practice of the week, but he was likely just having his reps managed after he had missed five straight games due to the knee injury before returning to action during this past Sunday's win over the Titans. With a full practice now under his belt, Sampson is in the clear to serve as the top change-of-pace option behind lead back Quinshon Judkins in this weekend's game against the Steelers.

items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Wicks (ankle) isn't participating in Thursday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.analysis: Wicks hasn't practiced in any fashion since Week 6 while he continues to manage an ankle injury. Unless he's able to get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Wicks will likely be ruled out for a second straight game this Sunday at Washington.

items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Spears (knee) isn't practicing Thursday, Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com reports.
items.analysis: Spears is sitting out a second consecutive practice, which doesn't bode well for his availability Sunday against the Bengals considering he was unable to suit up for the Week 7 loss to Cleveland. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to avoid being ruled out on the Titans' subsequent injury report.

items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Tate (shoulder) won't practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.analysis: Tate also sat out Wednesday due to this injury. The rookie fourth overall pick will have one more opportunity to practice in some capacity Friday ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals. If Tate sits out a game for the first time in his young career, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley (hip) could get more downfield targets while Wan'Dale Robinson runs his customary short and intermediate routes.

items.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) injury update
items.news: Coleman (ankle) rushed nine times for 54 yards and caught both of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Coleman led the team in carries in his return from injured reserve and finished second behind Bo Nix (73) in rushing yards. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey combined for just 29 rushing yards on nine rushing attempts, though Dobbins had a rushing touchdown and Harvey had a receiving touchdown. Coleman was notably the team's running back of choice as the Broncos ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, and head coach Sean Payton said after the game that the team has "got to get (Coleman) more touches," per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Denver will likely continue to utilize all three running backs in Week 8 against the Chiefs, but this was an encouraging performance for Coleman in the rookie fourth-round pick's first action since Week 2.

items.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Ferguson (ankle) won't return to practice this week, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
items.analysis: Coach Sean McVay revealed that Ferguson's practice window to return from injured reserve won't open during Week 8 prep. Ferguson has missed the minimum four games while on IR due to an ankle sprain, and for as long as he's sidelined, the Rams will continue to roll with Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen at tight end.

items.headline: Adam Randall (neck) nearing return from IR
items.news: The Ravens opened Randall's (neck) 21-day practice window Wednesday.
items.analysis: Randall was a full participant in his return to practice. The Ravens placed the running back on IR in late August with an undisclosed injury, which has now been revealed to be a neck issue. Randall's instant jump to full participation means the fifth-round rookie could be ready to suit up as soon as Sunday's game against the Bills.

items.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) ruled out
items.news: The Bills designated Shavers (knee) to return from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he will not play against the Ravens on Sunday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Shavers has progressed enough in his recovery from a torn ACL to return to practice, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Shavers saw his role in the Bills' offense steadily increase over the course of the 2025 season before suffering his injury in the wild-card round against the Jaguars in January. His next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9.

items.headline: Michael Briscoe listed as out
items.news: Briscoe is listed as out.

items.headline: Jaylin Noel (toe) placed on IR
items.news: Noel, who was placed on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, is expected to require surgery to address his toe injury and will miss the remainder of the season, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.analysis: Noel was forced out of this past Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants after going down with the toe injury with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The loss of Noel is a major blow to the Texans, as he had been serving as the team's top return man in addition to emerging as a big-play threat on offense. Through Houston's first seven games, Noel had recorded 19 receptions for a team-leading 331 yards and two touchdowns and added 26 yards on four carries.

items.headline: Marcus Mariota (knee) practice update
items.news: Mariota (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.analysis: Mariota was sidelined for the previous two games with a sprained MCL but is ready to resume QB2 duties coming out of the Commanders' bye. Athan Kaliakmanis should slide back down to the QB3 spot for Washington.

items.headline: Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) placed on IR
items.news: The Eagles placed Pierce (undisclosed) on injured reserve Wednesday
items.analysis: Pierce thus is joining fellow RBs Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) on IR, leaving Saquon Barkley and Jaydon Blue as the only players at the position on the Eagles' active roster. Pierce made a late exit from Monday's loss to the Cowboys, which followed Barkley's own earlier departure due to a back issue. Pierce's health concern is enough for him to miss at least four contests, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, in Arizona.

items.headline: Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR
items.news: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Adams had successful surgery on his left hamstring, and the Rams are hopeful that the wide receiver will be able to return on the early side of his 6-to-10-week recovery timetable, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.analysis: Adams tweaked his hamstring on the Rams' final offensive possession of a Week 6 loss to the Cardinals on Oct. 18, and McVay revealed one day later that the wide receiver had a rupture of the hamstring and required surgery, with the aim to return "a little after" the Rams' Week 11 bye. L.A. seems to be targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which is a shade more than six weeks from the initial injury. In any case, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell will continue to earn the WR reps behind top option Puka Nacua.

items.headline: Jaylen Wright (quadriceps/foot) practice update
items.news: Wright (quadriceps/foot) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Wright exited Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets late in the fourth quarter on account of the quad issue, but his availability for this weekend's game against the Patriots doesn't look to be in any peril. Since returning to action Week 4 against the Vikings following a one-game absence, Wright has been a clear second fiddle to Ollie Gordon out of the Miami backfield. In his last three appearances, Wright hasn't recorded any receptions and has logged no more than six carries in any contest.

items.headline: Erick All Jr. (ACL) remains on IR
items.news: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed Wednesday that All has been diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee and will require season-ending surgery, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
items.analysis: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

items.headline: Terry McLaurin (knee) placed on IR
items.news: The Commanders placed McLaurin (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: McLaurin's move to IR was merely a formality, as the 31-year-old wideout was recently diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee that will require season-ending surgery. The transaction clears a spot on the 53-man roster for fellow wideout Van Jefferson, whom the Commanders signed off their practice squad.

items.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: Bryant is on injured reserve with an ankle injury.

items.headline: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return in December, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
items.analysis: Stribling was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and remains on injured reserve. He missed a big opportunity for snaps and targets with the team dealing with so many injuries at the wide receiver position, but all indications are Stribling will be back for the stretch run and a possible trip to the playoffs.

items.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) nearing return from IR
items.news: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
items.analysis: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

items.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR
items.news: The Giants placed Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

items.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) remains on IR
items.news: Pittman is on injured reserve with a foot injury.

items.headline: Josh Kattus listed as out
items.news: Kattus is listed as out.

items.headline: Jalen Brooks (wrist) placed on IR
items.news: The Cardinals placed Brooks (wrist) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.analysis: The transaction comes after Brooks announced earlier in the day that he underwent season-ending wrist surgery. Brooks saw light snaps through the first four weeks of the season, but he stepped in as the Cardinals' No. 3 wideout for the past three games after Marvin Harrison was traded to the Texans. The 26-year-old will finish the 2026 campaign with five receptions for 81 yards on 17 targets to go with 499 yards on 19 kickoff returns.

items.headline: Luke Schoonmaker (groin) listed as questionable
items.news: Schoonmaker is listed as questionable with a groin injury.

items.headline: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Samuel (hamstring) has a chance to return following the 49ers' Week 8 bye, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.analysis: All three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Samuel and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) are eyeing a Week 9 return against the Raiders, so the 49ers' wide receiver depth chart could look vastly different coming out of the bye. Samuel would likely go back to his part-time role, handling short-area passes and an occasional handoff or two. He's not a particularly exciting fantasy play when Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) are all healthy.

items.headline: Christian McCaffrey (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: McCaffrey is dealing with a mild hamstring strain rather than a quadriceps injury, and the 49ers believe he'll be ready following the team's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SF Standard reports.
items.analysis: After McCaffrey briefly exited Sunday's loss to Atlanta with what had been described as a thigh issue, this update offers more clarity on the injury and a favorable outlook. The timing of the 49ers' bye gives the veteran running back added recovery time ahead of their next game in Week 9 versus the Raiders, though his practice status will still be worth monitoring once San Francisco returns to work. Kaelon Black will be a priority add off waivers considering CMC's injury history.

items.headline: Mike Evans (achilles) listed as questionable
items.news: Evans (Achilles) is expected to return after San Francisco's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SF Standard reports.
items.analysis: After missing Sunday's game against the Falcons with the Achilles issue, Evans appears to be trending toward a return for San Francisco's next contest in Week 9 against the Raiders. Working as the Niners' big-play X receiver this season, Evans has been nearly unstoppable when healthy. Maintaining health has been his biggest issue. When on the field, Evans is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside.

items.headline: James Conner (foot) remains on IR
items.news: When asked Monday if Conner (foot) will play this season, coach Mike LaFleur said "potentially," Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: It's a typical LaFleur non-answer type of answer. It was reported two weeks ago that Conner was close to practicing, but there's been no indication his 21-day practice window is close to being opened by the Cardinals. There's not much room on the depth chart for another running back that doesn't play special teams in Arizona.

items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) remains on IR
items.news: Brooks is on injured reserve while recovering from abdomen surgery.

items.headline: Britain Covey (knee) ruled out
items.news: Covey (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's contest versus the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Covey appeared to injure his knee during the opening kickoff Monday, and Philadelphia will now have to finish the game without him. All of his snaps so far this season have come on special teams, and Elijah Moore and Dameon Pierce are the next men up in the return game for the Eagles.

items.headline: Dillon Gabriel (back) activated
items.news: The Browns activated Gabriel (back) from injured reserve Monday.
items.analysis: Cleveland needed to make a decision on the quarterback after opening his 21-day practice window 20 days ago, so he'll now join the 53-man roster as one of the team's four quarterbacks. The Browns figure to make a move at the position in the near future, and perhaps they'll try to gauge trade interest in Gabriel.

items.headline: Tip Reiman (ankle) listed as out
items.news: Head coach Mike LaFleur stated he's "not too sure" if Reiman (ankle) will play this season, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.analysis: Reiman hasn't played this season and is currently on the reserve/PUP list. While there haven't been any updates on when the 25-year-old will be back on the field, it appears the door isn't fully closed regarding his return before the end of the 2026 campaign. Reiman has appeared in 21 regular-season games for the Cardinals since being drafted in the third round in the 2024 NFL Draft, amassing nine catches for 55 yards.

items.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan reiterated Monday that Robinson (ankle) has a chance to return following the team's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
items.analysis: Shanahan said the same thing 11 days ago, so the timeline appears to remain in place for Robinson, who suffered a high-ankle sprain way back in Week 2 against Miami. The Niners are expected to get plenty of reinforcements following their open date, and all three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Robinson could be among those returning for Week 9 against Las Vegas.

items.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) injury update
items.news: Douglas (ankle) caught two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Douglas made an immediate impact in his first action since Week 2. The rookie third-round pick capped the game's first drive with a seven-yard touchdown catch for his first NFL TD, then stayed in along the sideline to score again on a 63-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter. Miami utilizes a run-heavy approach when possible, but the Dolphins may be forced to throw more if they fall behind as expected in Week 8 against the Patriots, which could lead to more opportunities for Douglas.

items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: Skattebo is expected to "OK" after tweaking his hamstring on a 42-yard run in overtime during Sunday's 27-21 win over the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Skattebo's explosive run put the Giants within field-goal range before he was subbed out for Devin Singletary, who ran up the middle for a 30-yard score to seal the win on the very next play. Though he told Dan Graziano of ESPN.com after the game that he "felt something" in his hamstring that prompted him to slide down at the end of his run rather than being tackled to the ground, Skattebo doesn't sound like he'll require an MRI and should be ready to play in the Giants' next game Nov. 8 versus the Eagles following a Week 8 bye. After being limited to just six snaps in a Week 6 loss to the Saints following a string of poor outings to begin the campaign, Skattebo stepped back into a lead role out of the backfield in Sunday's victory and delivered his best performance of the season, finishing with 121 total yards and a touchdown on 18 touches.

items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains on IR
items.news: Tyson is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Woody Marks (leg) injury update
items.news: Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Mark remained busy in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), handling 20 touches while no other running back got a touch for the Texans. Over the last three games, the first of which Montgomery left early and the last two of which he missed, Marks has recorded 247 scrimmage yards on 56 touches. Marks missed some action in the second half Sunday due to a leg injury but returned to the game. Houston's Week 8 bye will give both Marks and Montgomery a chance to heal up, and Houston would likely return to a backfield platoon in Week 9 against the Chargers if Montgomery's ready to play.

items.headline: Myles Price (head) injury update
items.news: Price (head) was back on the field for the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Colts, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.analysis: Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

items.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Donaldson (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris.
items.analysis: Donaldson picked up the injury during the first quarter and has been taken to the locker room to undergo more tests on his shoulder injury. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller would be the remaining healthy running backs on the Saints active roster for the rest of Sunday's game if Donaldson is not cleared to return.

items.headline: Carter Runyon nearing return from IR
items.news: The Raiders have ruled out Runyon (foot) for Sunday's game against the Rams.
items.analysis: Runyon was a full participant in practice throughout the week, after he had been limited in the Raiders' three Week 6 sessions upon having his 21-day window opened Oct. 14. If the tight end can remain free of restrictions in practices during Week 8 prep, he'll stand a good chance of being activated from injured reserve ahead of the Raiders' Nov. 1 matchup with the Jets.

items.headline: Tyler Badie (thumb) nearing return from IR
items.news: The Broncos placed Badie (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

items.headline: Beaux Collins ruled out
items.news: Collins (hip) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: Collins was looking to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 but has not recovered enough from his hip injury to suit up. The wide receiver must be activated from IR by Nov. 12, or he will spend the entirety of the 2026 season confined to the list.

items.headline: Brashard Smith (hamstring) placed on IR
items.news: The Chiefs placed Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.analysis: Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

items.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) ruled out
items.news: Johnson (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Johnson's lack of participation in Friday's practice session appears to have been indicative of his playing status for Sunday's contest. The tight end will not be able to overcome his neck injury in time for Week 7 and will have to look toward the Giants' Week 9 contest against the Eagles after the bye.

items.headline: Brevin Jordan (foot) injury update
items.news: Jordan (foot) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.analysis: Jordan likely sustained his foot injury during Thursday's practice, but the tight end was quickly able to upgrade to a full participant in Friday's practice. Jordan is all set to suit up as a depth option at tight end in Sunday's contest.

items.headline: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Friday that Arroyo (shoulder) underwent surgery and will likely be out for the rest of the season, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
items.analysis: Macdonald didn't outright rule Arroyo out for the entire 2026 campaign, leaving the possibility that the second-year tight end would be available if the Seahawks made a deep playoff run. Regardless, Arroyo will not be available for the rest of the regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, leaving Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup as the Seahawks' depth options at tight end behind AJ Barner.

items.headline: Cole Kmet (knee) placed on IR
items.news: The Bears placed Kmet (knee) on injured reserve Friday.
items.analysis: Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday. Even with the emergence of Colston Loveland, Kmet was still a key piece in Chicago's offense as a run blocker, and he'll end his 2026 regular season with a 10-87-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) across seven games. Rookie third-rounder Sam Roush is the only other healthy tight end on the 53-man roster other than Loveland, so the Bears could look to bolster the position group by trade or free agency.

items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) injury update
items.news: Montgomery (groin) isn't expected to play Sunday against the Giants, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.analysis: Montgomery is poised to miss a second straight game, and with Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured on the practice squad after he was elevated for Week 6, the Texans will ride Woody Marks and special-teamer Dare Ogunbowale out of the backfield, with Marks likely to see virtually every meaningful carry versus New York.

items.headline: Luke Musgrave on PUP list
items.news: Musgrave is on the PUP list.

items.headline: Matt Hibner (hand) practice update
items.news: Hibner (hand) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Hibner managed a full practice Thursday for the first time since he hurt his hand back in Week 5 at Atlanta, suggesting he'll more than likely be available in Week 7 versus the Bengals. Before getting hurt, he was operating as Baltimore's secondary tight end, filling a complementary role relative to veteran starter Mark Andrews.

items.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) remains on IR
items.news: Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury.

items.headline: Jaylin Lane (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: Lane underwent surgery Oct. 9 to repair his fractured and dislocated ankle, and he is expected to be cleared for activities before OTAs, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
items.analysis: Lane sustained his season-ending ankle injury during the Commanders' Week 4 win against the Colts, and the injury was severe enough for him to stay in London overnight to be monitored and undergo additional tests. His absence has opened the door to more playing time for both Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, and they are both candidates for another bump in playing time after Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.

items.headline: Colbie Young (knee) injury update
items.news: Young (knee) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
items.analysis: Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.
